title: Karan Johar Says He Is Dissuading Twins Yash And Roohi From Bollywood
excerpt: On Koffee With Karan, the filmmaker said the industry is tough and he will be too old to protect his children when they are ready — a view Kareena Kapoor gently pushed back on.
body:
• Karan Johar said he is almost dissuading his twins, Yash and Roohi, from joining Bollywood.
  • “It's not an easy place. It's tough,” he said on Koffee With Karan, adding he will be too old to protect them at that time.
  • Kareena Kapoor offered a different view, suggesting protection itself can become the issue and parents sometimes have to let children go.
  • Yash and Roohi were welcomed via surrogacy in February 2017; neither child has announced any plan to enter films.

Filmmaker Karan Johar, who heads Dharma Productions and has launched some of Hindi cinema's biggest stars, says he is actively discouraging his own children from entering the business he has spent his life in.

Johar discussed parenting with actors Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan on an episode of Koffee With Karan, according to Filmfare and India Weekly.

“I will be too old to protect them”

“Well, look, as I said, it's not an easy place. It's tough. I am almost dissuading my children from the business. And everybody says, 'Why are you doing that? Why are you doing that?' I am like, look, I will be too old to protect them at that time,” Johar said.

The comment was about his own fear as a parent, not a decision by his children. Yash and Roohi are nine years old, and neither has publicly announced any plan to become an actor or work in films. Johar has also not said he would stop them if, as adults, they chose the industry themselves.

What he described was timing: by the time the twins are old enough to start a career and face the scrutiny that comes with it, he worries he will not be able to shield or guide them the way a younger parent in the industry might.

Kareena Kapoor's counterpoint

Kareena Kapoor offered a contrasting take in the same conversation. “But I feel maybe the protection is also what is causing the issue. I think sometimes we just have to, like, probably just... you know, we're all so protective towards our children,” she said.

She recalled how their own parents had taken a looser approach: “I feel sometimes our parents just let us go and say, 'Karni hai toh karo, you know, karo. You have to go and 'ragdo.'”

Filmfare reported Johar quietly agreed with her point, acknowledging that balancing a protective instinct with the industry's hard realities is an ongoing struggle. The exchange set two approaches side by side — protect children from difficulty in advance, or let them learn by meeting it — without resolving which is right.

A film family, a different wish for the next generation

Johar is the son of veteran producer Yash Johar and has carried forward his father's legacy through Dharma Productions, one of Hindi cinema's leading production houses. He welcomed twins Yash and Roohi via surrogacy in February 2017 as a single father.

Yash was named after his late father, while Roohi's name is an anagram of his mother Hiroo Johar's name, India Weekly noted.

That lineage is what makes the remarks notable. Johar is not an outsider warning against Bollywood; he is one of its central figures, closely associated with star launches and with the public debate over nepotism that has followed his career. His caution therefore reads less as criticism of any individual and more as a parent's account of the emotional toll and relentless scrutiny he knows first-hand.

For now, it remains a father's stated preference while his children are still in primary school. Whether Yash and Roohi eventually choose film, another profession, or something entirely outside public life will be their decision — and, on Kareena's argument in the same episode, perhaps one they will need room to make for themselves.
